findings.fix: Remove user-scalable=no (and any maximum-scale restriction) from the viewport meta tag so users can zoom.
findings.location: The viewport meta tag in the document head, id="head-viewport"
findings.violation: user-scalable=no disables pinch to zoom, which prevents users with low vision from zooming the page even though the viewport is otherwise responsive.

findings.evidence: style="color:#999999" on the text "Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk..."
findings.fix: Remove the inline color override or replace it with a darker color that reaches at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against the background, such as #595959.
findings.location: First paragraph of the "Accessibility improvements" section, id="s1-p1"
findings.violation: Gray text at #999999 on the page's default white background produces a contrast ratio of roughly 2.85 to 1, well below the WCAG AA minimum of 4.5 to 1 for normal size text.

findings.evidence: The sentence "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." appears verbatim in all three, attached to unrelated topics: kiosk schedules, mobile app fare adjustments, and online portal service issue reports.
findings.fix: Write a distinct, topic specific closing sentence for each paragraph, or remove the repeated sentence where it adds no information.
findings.location: Paragraphs id="s1-p1", id="s1-p2", and the status card text id="s3-statuscard"
findings.violation: The same boilerplate sentence is copy pasted across unrelated paragraphs, so the content reads as templated filler rather than information specific to each section.

findings.evidence: The table opens directly with <tr><th scope="col">Zone</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr> and has no caption anywhere in its markup.
findings.fix: Add a caption element inside the table, for example "Zone status", describing its contents.
findings.location: Table id="s2-table1" in the "Schedule changes" section
findings.violation: The table has no caption element, so a screen reader user navigating to the table gets no description of what it contains before reaching its data cells.

findings.fix: Replace the fixed pixel width with a relative or max width value, such as max-width:960px; width:100%.
findings.location: The promo banner div id="s3-banner", class "promo-banner", in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: A hard coded 960px width does not shrink on narrower viewports, which will cause horizontal overflow or clipping on mobile screens given the page's device-width viewport setting.

findings.fix: Remove the fixed height and let the box size to its content, or use min-height:60px without overflow:hidden.
findings.location: The status card div id="s3-statuscard", class "status-card"
findings.violation: A fixed 60px height combined with overflow:hidden will clip the paragraph text inside it whenever the text wraps to more lines than fit, including at larger browser font sizes or zoom levels.

findings.evidence: <div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">
findings.fix: Replace the div with a native button element, for example button type="button" aria-label="Delete item", which gets correct keyboard and role semantics for free.
findings.location: The delete control div id="s3-customcontrol", class "icon-delete"
findings.violation: This interactive delete control is built from a div with role="button" instead of a native button element, and the document contains no script anywhere that would give it keyboard activation on Enter or Space, or a click handler.

findings.evidence:
Choose a plan
and two sibling divs with the same bare structure and no other markup.
findings.fix: Mark the steps up as an ordered list and add aria-current="step" to whichever step is active.
findings.location: The wizard steps container id="s3-wizard" and its three child step divs (s3-step1, s3-step2, s3-step3)
findings.violation: The three steps are plain, unnumbered divs with no list semantics and no indication of which step is current, so assistive technology users get no sense of progress or structure.

findings.evidence: read the accessibility improvements list, inside the sentence "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, read the accessibility improvements list."
findings.fix: Change the link text to match the destination, for example "read the fare adjustment history."
findings.location: The link in paragraph id="s3-linkpara", link id="s3-link1"
findings.violation: The link text promises an "accessibility improvements list" but the href points to /fares/history and the surrounding sentence is about upcoming adjustments, so the link text does not describe its actual destination.

findings.evidence: <label for="topic-alt" id="s3-form-topic-label">Route</label> immediately followed by <select id="topic">
findings.fix: Change the label's for attribute to "topic" (or change the select's id to "topic-alt") so they match.
findings.location: Form id="s3-form", label id="s3-form-topic-label" paired with the select id="topic"
findings.violation: The label's for attribute points to "topic-alt" but the select element's id is "topic", so the two do not match and the "Route" label is not programmatically associated with the dropdown; clicking the label will not focus it and screen readers will not announce "Route" for the field.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label">Phone number (required)</label> next to <input id="phone" type="tel">
findings.fix: Add required (or aria-required="true") to the phone input so its programmatic state matches its visible label text.
findings.location: Form id="s3-form", label id="s3-form-phone-label" paired with input id="phone"
findings.violation: The label text tells sighted users the phone field is required, but the input itself has no required attribute or aria-required="true", so screen readers and native form validation do not treat it as required.

findings.evidence: followed by Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the promo input.
findings.location: Form id="s3-form", input id="promo" and its error message id="s3-form-promo-error"
findings.violation: The promo input is flagged invalid with aria-invalid="true", but nothing in its markup points to the error message, so screen reader users are told the field is invalid without ever hearing why.
